{{Short description|Japanese mathematician}}
'''Hisashi Okamoto''' (岡本 久, ''Okamoto Hisashi'', born 23 November 1956)<ref>{{cite web|title=Okamoto Hisashi 岡本 久|website=National Institute of Informatics, Japan|url=https://nrid.nii.ac.jp/nrid/1000040143359/}}</ref> is a Japanese applied mathematician, specializing in mathematical [[fluid mechanics]] and [[computational fluid dynamics]].<ref name=homepage>{{cite web|title=Hisashi Okamoto|website=Kyoto University, Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences|url=http://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~okamoto/}}</ref>

Okamoto graduated from the University of Tokyo in March 1979. In April 1981 he became a research associate to Hiroshi Fujita (known for the Fujita-Kato theorem<ref>{{cite journal|author=Okamoto, H.|author2=Kato, T.|authorlink2=Tosio Kato|title=On the Navier-Stokes initial value problem. I|journal=Archive for Rational Mechanics and Analysis|volume=16|year=1964|issue=4|pages=269–315|doi=10.1007/BF00276188|bibcode=1964ArRMA..16..269F|s2cid=122166828}}</ref>) at the University of Tokyo. There in 1985 he received his Doctorate of Science with Fujita as advisor. For the academic year 1986–1987 Okamoto was a visiting fellow at the [[University of Minnesota]]'s Institute for Mathematics and Its Applications. In August 1987 Okamoto became an associate professor in the University of Tokyo's Department of Applied Science. In 1988 he visited the [[National University of Singapore]]. At [[Kyoto University]]'s [[Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences]] (RIMS), he became an associate professor in April 1990 and a full professor in April 1994. At RIMS he was Head of the Computer Science Research Laboratory from 2004 to 2005 and deputy director in 2006, 2009, and 2011.<ref name=CV>{{cite web|title=CV of Hisashi Okamoto|website=Kyoto University, Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences|url=http://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~okamoto/cv.html}}</ref> He is editor-in-chief of the ''Japan Journal of Industrial and Applied Mathematics'' (JJIAM).<ref name=homepage/>

Okamoto is the author or co-author of over 100 articles in refereed journals or in books of conference proceedings.<ref>{{cite web|title=Research Papers, Hisashi Okamoto|website=Kyoto University, Research Institute for Mathematical Sciences|url=http://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~okamoto/paper/paper2.htm}} (including online links to publications)</ref> He wrote, with Mayumi Shōji, the 2001 monograph ''The mathematical theory of permanent progressive water-waves''.<ref>{{cite book|author1=Okamoto, Hisashi|author2=Shōji, Mayumi|title=The Mathematical Theory of Permanent Progressive Water-waves|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=D4e-UfG974MC|year=2001|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-02-4450-7}}</ref><ref name="Vanden-Broeck2003">{{cite journal|last1=Vanden-Broeck|first1=J. M.|title=Review of ''The Mathematical Theory of Permanent Progressive Water-Waves'' by H. Okamoto & M. Shōji|journal=Journal of Fluid Mechanics|volume=474|year=2003|pages=410–411|issn=0022-1120|doi=10.1017/S0022112002002951|s2cid=122573566}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
* 1998 — Invited Speaker, International Congress of Mathematicians, Berlin 1998<ref>{{cite book|author=Okamoto, Hisashi|chapter=A Study of Bifurcation of Kolmogorov Flows with an Emphasis on the Singular Limit|title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, 1998, Berlin|volume=3|pages=513–522|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011607000}}</ref>
* 2002 — Inoue Science Award
* 2011 — President of the East Asia SIAM, 2011–2012
* 2013 — Fellow of the Japan Society of Fluid Mechanics
* 2013 — Fellow of the Japan Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics
* 2015 — Plenary Lecturer, Mathematical Society of Japan, September 2015.
* 2016 — Hiroshi Fujiwara Prize on Mathematical Science
